rce, returning the existing waiver |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `null`. Read
able by anyone who can view the run |\n| `DELETE .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putting the gat
e back. Idempotent; a second call reports the original revocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterat
ions` | Per-iteration results: tool calls, token usage, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/{iterationI
d}/trace` | Full trace: messages + expected-vs-actual analysis |\n| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs for a suite
, newest first |\n\n**Eval result ingestion** (`/projects/{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`): how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves results from eval
runs executed outside the platform (local dev, CI). The `{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the key org's Def
ault project. Most users never call these directly; set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/concep

ts/saving-results.md) does:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: create a run fr
om finished results and finalize it |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently reuse) a run by
`externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/iterations` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST .../eval-inge
st/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (idempotent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's raw bytes (wi
dget HTML too large to send inline) and return its `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Retired. Answers
`410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST .../eval-ing

est/artifacts` instead |

**Agent** (`/projects/{projectId}/agent`): a headless assistant turn for
building conversational surf

aces:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../agent` | Run ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: "
user\"\\|\"assistant\", content}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 96 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to
the project. The turn can read project servers/suites/runs and **create eval suites**; it can NOT start runs: kick those off yours
elf with `POST .../eval-runs`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, the `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links),
and token `usage`. Capped at 4 concurrent turns per organization and \\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent; never blind-retry**: d
edupe on your own trigger identity, and on an error response check `details.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list su

ites) before retrying, or you'll create duplicates |

**Studies** (`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it

does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environme
nt it publishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspace membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, ne

ver null |

**Swarms, authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,
`.../swarms...`): the definitions a swa
rm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is an aut
horing container holding defaults for the goals made\nunder it. Nothing here starts anything; launching is\n`POST .../goals/{goalI

d}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../personas` |
Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{personaI
d}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. *
*409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accep
ts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PATCH .../
goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `DELETE ..
./goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal; existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms` | List s
warm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | On
e swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade; existing goals keep their own values |

| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |

**Swarms, generation**. Drafts a
model writes for you. Both routes return\ncandidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create\nroutes abo

ve. Neither accepts an `Idempotency-Key`, and retries return
different drafts.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST
.../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `P

OST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
>
The generation routes consume **no customer credits** (the model cost is on\n> MCPJam). They are still subject to usage limits, an
d each limit means a\n> different wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generatio
n quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform
_capacity\"`, resets at UTC midnight). All three carry\n> `Retry-After`. Honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `fal

se`
> on every one: buying credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

*
*Swarms, runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,\n`.../goal-runs/...`): launching a goal and reading what it produced

:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |
| `POST .../goals
/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers `202`; the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSpon
sored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_c
hanged`) and nothing is created. The response can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runI
d}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sess
ions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent; a second can

cel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always
send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Re
playing a key\n returns the original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the
header is read as a request that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before rep
orting a failure.** A stopped run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a s
tatus of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, no
t `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two\

n targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
> sessio
ns. Two different `429`s can come back; the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets

at UTC midnight).
> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms, insights**: what a ru
n revealed. Read these in order of cost: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry\naggrega
